stem: A client asks why the clinician is using the FRAX calculator in addition to reviewing bone-density results. Which explanation by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: FRAX estimates 10-year fracture probability using multiple clinical risk factors and can incorporate femoral-neck bone mineral density when available; it is not based on bone density alone.
options.B: FRAX uses only the DXA T-score, so age, prior fracture, smoking, glucocorticoid exposure, and other clinical factors do not affect the calculation.
options.C: FRAX is a genetic test that estimates fracture risk from inherited variants without using clinical history.
options.D: FRAX replaces clinical judgment because every risk factor is modeled in complete dose- and severity-specific detail.

rationale: A is correct. The current official FRAX/FRAXplus calculator estimates 10-year fracture probability using individualized clinical risk factors including age, sex, weight, height, previous fracture, parental hip fracture, smoking, glucocorticoid use, rheumatoid arthritis, secondary osteoporosis, and alcohol use, with femoral-neck BMD entered when available. The calculator can also be used without a BMD value. B incorrectly reduces FRAX to bone density alone. C misclassifies FRAX as genetic testing. D is incorrect because official FRAX documentation notes important limitations: several risk factors are entered as yes/no variables and dose-response or fracture-number/severity effects are not fully represented, so clinical judgment remains necessary. The final item emphasizes what FRAX adds beyond DXA while avoiding unsupported treatment thresholds or country-specific intervention cutoffs.
educational_objective: Explain that FRAX combines multiple clinical risk factors with optional femoral-neck BMD to estimate 10-year fracture probability and should be interpreted alongside clinical judgment rather than as a bone-density-only or fully comprehensive model.
source_organization: FRAX / FRAXplus, Centre for Metabolic Bone Diseases, University of Sheffield
source_document_title: FRAXplus Calculation Tool; FRAX Calculation Tool and FAQ
source_version_date: Current FRAXplus/FRAX web calculators accessed 2026-08-18; FRAXplus identified by the legacy FRAX site as the most up-to-date calculator platform
source_locator: FRAXplus 'Calculation Tool' → Questionnaire: age, sex, weight, height, previous fracture, parent fractured hip, current smoking, glucocorticoids, rheumatoid arthritis, secondary osteoporosis, alcohol and optional femoral-neck BMD; introductory text: FRAX integrates clinical risk factors with or without BMD to calculate ten-year fracture probability. FRAX FAQ/Notes on risk factors → dose-response for prior fractures, smoking, glucocorticoids and alcohol is not fully captured and clinical judgment is needed.
source_claim_supported: Current official FRAX/FRAXplus resources directly support the multivariable inputs, optional femoral-neck BMD, 10-year probability purpose, and limitations requiring clinical judgment.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity → Reduction of Risk Potential: interpret diagnostic and risk-assessment findings, compare client data with expected findings, and educate clients regarding factors that influence future physiologic risk.
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source's generic FRAX-description item using the current official FRAXplus/FRAX calculator. The final version accurately distinguishes multivariable risk estimation from BMD-only assessment and explicitly preserves clinical judgment instead of implying the calculator models every exposure in full detail.
audit_findings: The source correctly stated that FRAX combines clinical factors and BMD but relied on a generic foundation source and omitted important model limitations.
Fresh official FRAXplus review directly verifies the complete core questionnaire and optional femoral-neck BMD input.
Official FRAX documentation also states that dose-response for several risk factors is not fully modeled, preserving the need for clinical judgment.
Distractors test BMD-only assessment, genetic-test misclassification and calculator-as-complete-replacement-for-judgment; none is defensible.
